'''Gordon George Wallace'''  is a scientist in the field of electromaterials. His students and collaborators use of [[nanotechnology]] in conjunction with organic conductors for energy conversion and storage as well as medical [[bionics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.electromaterials.edu.au/about/|title=ARC Centre of Excellence for Electromaterials Science|website=www.electromaterials.edu.au|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref> He has developed approaches to fabrication that allow material properties discovered in the nano world to be translated into micro structures and macro scopic devices.

Wallace's research interests include new materials and the use of these in energy and biomedical devices.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.electromaterials.edu.au/people-directory/professor-gordon-wallace2/|title=Professor Gordon Wallace - Our People - ARC Centre of Excellence for Electromaterials Science|website=www.electromaterials.edu.au|access-date=2017-05-19|archive-date=1 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170401114607/http://www.electromaterials.edu.au/people-directory/professor-gordon-wallace2/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Wallace is currently Director of the Intelligent Polymer Research Institute<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Gordon G. Wallace |url=http://ipri.uow.edu.au/people/UOW001346.html |access-date=2017-05-19 |website=ipri.uow.edu.au |language=en-au |archive-date=2 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170602053405/http://ipri.uow.edu.au/people/UOW001346.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the former Director of the [[Australian National Fabrication Facility]] (Materials Node)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Materials Node {{!}} www.anff.org.au |url=http://www.anff.org.au/materials-node.html |access-date=2017-05-19 |website=www.anff.org.au |language=en |archive-date=29 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170529214025/http://www.anff.org.au/materials-node.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> both headquartered at the [[University of Wollongong]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=University of Wollongong, Australia |url=http://www.uow.edu.au/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160415214448/http://www.uow.edu.au/index.html |archive-date=15 April 2016 |access-date=2017-05-19 |website=www.uow.edu.au}}</ref> He was also previously Executive Research Director at the ARC Centre of Excellence for Electromaterials Science<ref name=":0" /> as well as Director of the [https://www.tricep.com.au/ Translational Research Initiative for Cellular Engineering and Printing (TRICEP)].

== Career==
Wallace graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] [[Honours degree|Honours]] ([[chemistry]] and [[physics]]) in 1979 and then received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1983. {{cn|date=March 2025}}

He was awarded an [[Australian Research Council]] QEII Fellowship in 1991, an ARC Senior Research Fellowship in 1995, an ARC Professorial Fellowship in 2002 and a Federation Fellowship in 2006.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Conductive electroactive polymers intelligent polymer systems|last=G.|first=Wallace, Gordon|date=2009|publisher=CRC|isbn=978-1-4200-6715-6|pages=xiii|oclc=851042729}}</ref> He was awarded a [[Doctor of Science|DSc]] from Deakin University in 2000.{{Cn|date=March 2025}}

== Research years ==
Wallace asserted that this instability could, if understood, be directed and controlled, allowing the creation of "intelligent" polymers – materials that sense and respond to stimuli.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tedxuwollongong.com/gordon-wallace/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120514054518/http://www.tedxuwollongong.com/gordon-wallace/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=14 May 2012|title=Professor Gordon Wallace {{!}} TEDxUWollongong|website=tedxuwollongong.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref>

In September 2008, Wallace's team moved to research facilities at the University of Wollongong's new Innovation Campus based at [[North Wollongong, New South Wales|North Wollongong]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/613992/new-innovation-campus-centre-will-reshape-world/|title=New Innovation Campus centre will reshape world|last=SHAW|first=EMMA|date=2009-03-08|work=Illawarra Mercury|access-date=2017-05-19|language=en}}</ref>

He published the book ''Organic Bionics''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Organic bionics|last=G.|first=Wallace, Gordon|date=2012|publisher=Wiley-VCH|isbn=978-3-527-32882-6|oclc=850975416}}</ref> He has an h index of 110 and has amassed in excess of 60,000 citations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7202483095|title=Scopus preview - Scopus - Author details (Wallace, Gordon G.)|website=www.scopus.com|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref> 

==Awards and honours==

* Wallace was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering|Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]] in 2003 and of the [[Australian Academy of Science]] in 2007.{{Cn|date=March 2025}}
* He was appointed as an [[Officer of the Order of Australia]] and Wollongong's [[Australia Day Ambassador]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/4426980/meet-the-illawarras-australia-day-honours-recipients/|title=Meet the Illawarra's Australia Day honours recipients|last=Media|first=Australian Community Media - Fairfax|date=2017-01-26|work=Illawarra Mercury|access-date=2017-05-19|language=en}}</ref>

* Later that year Wallace was named [[NSW Scientist of the Year]].<ref>[http://www.chiefscientist.nsw.gov.au/premiersprizes/2017-nsw-scientist-of-the-year 2017 NSW Scientist of the Year] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201034021/http://www.chiefscientist.nsw.gov.au/premiersprizes/2017-nsw-scientist-of-the-year |date=1 December 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chiefscientist.nsw.gov.au/premiersprizes/2017-nsw-scientist-of-the-year|title=2017 NSW Scientist of the Year - NSW Chief Scientist & Engineer|website=www.chiefscientist.nsw.gov.au|language=en|access-date=2017-11-27|archive-date=1 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201034021/http://www.chiefscientist.nsw.gov.au/premiersprizes/2017-nsw-scientist-of-the-year}}</ref>

* He received the Inaugural Polymer Science and Technology award from the [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]] (RACI) in 1992. He was awarded an ETS Walton Fellowship by [[Science Foundation Ireland]] in 2003. In 2009 he was awarded a lifetime achievement award by [[SPIE]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://spie.org/about-spie/press-room/press-releases/ss09-preview-3-3-09|title=Infrastructure, health, entertainment technologies to be advanced at SPIE Smart Structures/NDE|website=spie.org|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref>

* He was appointed to the Prime Ministers Knowledge Nation 100 in 2015. He received the [[Eureka Prizes|Eureka Prize]] for Leadership in Science and Innovation in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/academy-congratulates-2016-eureka-prize-winners|title=Academy congratulates 2016 Eureka Prize winners {{!}} Australian Academy of Science|website=www.science.org.au|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2016-08-31/eureka-prize-2016/7784746|title=5 of the coolest things we spotted at Eureka Prize 2016|date=2016-08-31|work=ABC News|access-date=2017-05-19|language=en-AU}}</ref>

* Australian Research Council (ARC) [[Australian Laureate Fellowship|Laureate Fellowship]], 2011<ref name="laureate">{{cite news |url=http://www.researchcareer.com.au/archived-news/australian-laureate-fellows-for-2011-announced |title=Australian Laureate Fellows for 2011 announced |date=10 August 2011 |work=Research Career |access-date=3 May 2020 }}</ref>
* Honorary member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Admittance Day 2023 |url=https://www.ria.ie/news/membership/admittance-day-2023 |website=www.ria.ie |publisher=Royal Irish Academy |access-date=27 May 2023 |archive-date=4 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204092303/https://www.ria.ie/news/membership/admittance-day-2023 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
